plain.text: Has God rejected his people? By no means! Paul himself is an Israelite. In Elijah's day, when Elijah thought he was the only faithful one left, God had kept seven thousand who had not worshipped Baal. So too, at the present time there is a remnant chosen by grace. And if it is by grace, then it is no longer by works. The rest were hardened, as Scripture says.

Did Israel stumble so as to fall beyond recovery? Not at all! Because of their stumbling, salvation has come to the Gentiles, to make Israel jealous. If their loss means riches for the world, how much more will their full inclusion mean! Paul uses the picture of an olive tree. Some natural branches were broken off, and wild olive branches (Gentile believers) were grafted in. Gentile believers must not be proud: they stand by faith, supported by the root. God is able to graft the natural branches back in.

Paul does not want them to be ignorant of a mystery: Israel has experienced a hardening in part until the full number of the Gentiles has come in, "and in this way all Israel will be saved". As far as the gospel is concerned, they are enemies for your sake, but as far as election is concerned, they are loved because of the patriarchs. God's gifts and his call can never be withdrawn. God has bound everyone over to disobedience so that he may have mercy on them all.

Paul bursts into praise: "Oh, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable his judgements, and his paths beyond tracing out! Who has known the mind of the Lord? For from him and through him and to him are all things. To him be the glory forever! Amen."

summary.bigIdea: God has not rejected Israel; his plan includes both Jews and Gentiles, and his wisdom is beyond our understanding.
points: God has kept a faithful remnant, chosen by grace.
Gentile believers are like wild branches grafted into God's olive tree, and must not be proud.
God's gifts and call are irrevocable, and his ways lead Paul to praise.
summary.reflection: Paul ends hard questions with worship. How might praise help you when you cannot understand everything?
